text:
jamal: quick sync — thinking about a change to how we build dashboard panels: enforce RBAC at the query planner layer instead of post-filtering in the projection. tradeoffs below.
priya: curious, why move it earlier? post-filtering has been simplest for incremental rollout.
jamal: main reasons: 1) avoid wasted work on heavy aggregations, 2) more accurate cost-estimates during planning, 3) easier to reason about SLOs for panels when we can short-circuit at planning time.
zoe: sounds promising but risky for correctness. can we guarantee parity with current post-filtering logic? edge cases: row-level policies, column redaction rules.
jamal: good call — we would keep a compatibility mode that mirrors current behavior for a percentage of tenants for a few weeks.
arun: perf-wise, earlier enforcement reduces CPU for large joins but adds complexity to planner. we'd need ability to annotate plan nodes with auth-guards and pushdown predicates.
priya: how would that interact with cached tiles/materialized panel results? if we change enforcement point, cached tiles might become invalid for some tenants.
jamal: plan: add cache key namespace that includes an auth-hash of the effective permissions. that keeps tiles correct but increases cache cardinality.
zoe: cache blowup worries me. can we combine auth-hash with tenant bucketization? like `auth-hash:v2` only for tenants with dynamic row policies.
jamal: yes — heuristic: only include auth-hash for tenants flagged as "policy-dynamic". others use tenant-only key.
priya: rollout strategy? prefer canary by tenant size.
arun: propose staging rollout: 1) planner changes in a feature flag (no enforcement), 2) enable enforcement for small internal tenants, 3) enable cache-keying + telemetry, 4) gradual ramp.
jamal: telemetry checklist I think we need:
- per-panel render time (p50/p95) before/after
- CPU tokens spent per panel
- cache hit rate by cache-key-type
- mismatches between old post-filtered results and new planner-filtered results (sampled)
- auth-path latency (time to compute effective permissions)
priya::+1: add also an incident hook if sampled mismatch rate > 0.1% for more than 5m.
zoe: how do we sample without leaking PII in telemetry? some policies include row-level identifiers.
jamal: telemetry will only report a deterministic digest (sha256) of the predicate tree, no raw values. and we store samples encrypted for compliance team.
arun: implementation notes:
```
// planner node annotation
struct AuthGuard { policy_id: string, pushdown_predicate: Expr }
plan_node.annotate(AuthGuard)
// during execution, if guard is present -> apply short-circuit
```
priya: any change for the query language surface? will SDKs need to change?
jamal: no SDK change. this is internal planner rework. APIs and routes remain identical.
zoe: what about evals and regression tests? we need deterministic suites for approx-equality and a ledger of known differences.
jamal: create an "auth-planner" eval shard that runs daily against curated datasets and flagged tenants.
priya: error handling: if planner mis-evaluates and throws, fall back to post-filter with a safe flag. fallback should be transparent and logged.
jamal: yes — fallback policy: catch planner auth errors -> record incident metric -> rerun with legacy post-filtering path.
deploy-bot: deployment note: new planner feature flag toggles in config-service. rolling restart of console-query-workers required.
arun: ops concern: during rollout we'll double-run some queries (planner path + fallback) for sampling — ensure throttles are in place or we'll spike cost.
jamal: agree — throttle sampling to <1% of traffic initially. also use off-peak windows for heavier sampling.
zoe: final QA ask: pair review for the plan and a short doc for security reviewers on predicate digesting.
priya: I can take the security doc draft.
jamal: thanks — I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with flags + telemetry dashboard skeleton. assigning followups:
- jamal: PR for planner annotations + feature flag
- arun: cache key change and ops runbook
- priya: security telemetry doc + sample handling
- zoe: eval shard + test cases

jamal: timeline: aim for canary in 3 weeks, general ramp 6–8 weeks assuming no major mismatches.
priya: sounds reasonable. tagging infra calendar for restart slot.
zoe: good! :rocket:
